endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Govern agentic memory: if the agent maintains persistent memory across sessions, that memory store must be brought under formal data governance (access controls, retention policies, BAA coverage).

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether a standard AI contract addendum, clause library, checklist, or audit of existing vendor contracts reduces gaps in AI-specific protections, and no study was supplied that documents the gap itself. The recommendation rests on one framework endorsement from CHAI, which addresses a narrower point about bringing persistent agent memory under data governance and BAA coverage.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty for effect cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The single CHAI endorsement is expert guidance, and it speaks to agentic memory governance rather than to contract addenda or audits in general, so it is also indirect to the recommendation as written.

The CHAI playbook states that an agent's persistent memory store must fall under access controls, retention policies, and BAA coverage. This suggests that existing BAA templates may not anticipate data held by AI agents across sessions. The endorsement does not specify clause language, audit methods, or update intervals, so organizations would need to draft those terms without a tested model.

commentary.research_gap: No study has compared organizations that use a standard AI contract addendum or audit vendor contracts for AI terms with organizations that do not. Useful studies would measure how often baseline contracts and BAAs lack AI-specific provisions, whether an addendum and audit change the terms that vendors accept, how long audits take and what they cost, and whether revised terms are followed by fewer data-use disputes or privacy incidents involving AI vendors.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may have less legal staff to draft and audit contracts, and whether a shared clause library narrows or widens that difference remains untested.
